The rendered file: lines (:625), the SCOPE file count, the lane decision from `files.length` (:408-409) and the `scope_paths` of the Cloudflare run all omit that changed file. A ticket-scoped hunt (the default depth is quick) can then report on a change set that leaves out the file the author named in a non-ASCII way. Full-audit mode uses walk() and is not affected. redact() misses JSON-style secrets (`"password": "x"`, `{"token":"x"}`), a private key block without its END line, quoted values with spaces, and any encoded form; it is defense in depth only and must not be the control for any content the container can reach beyond what the agent can already read.

The container mounts the whole repository including .git (MASK_SKIP, :40): .git/config can hold a remote URL with basic-auth credentials (`https://user:pass@host` is not redacted) and the full history. The agent can read the same files, so no new reader, but a clone with an embedded credential would reach the committed artifact. Consider masking .git/config.

KEY_RE does not match `.envrc`, `.htpasswd`, `credentials.json`, `*.tfvars` or `terraform.tfstate`, and the mask walk skips node_modules; the shared rule is peer-owned (h1-guardrail), noted here only because maskPaths depends on it.
